hybrid: Ranks 1-3 are the three prose uses of the word (the Anthropic ASL row, the section 2.2.2 expert-disagreement paragraph, the section 3.4 'to avoid catastrophic harm' sentence), in near the right order: the literal phrase 'catastrophic risk' occurs only in the ASL row, so it is first. The grade-2 passage the Report's most extreme outcome ('marginalisation or extinction of humanity', the loss-of-control Key information bullet, #271) does not use the word and is not in the top 20. The six grade-1 passages not in the top 20 are the summaries and neighbouring severity vocabulary ('could be severe', 'severe harm', 'mass harm'); that is a fair miss for a lexical-semantic fusion. Ranks 4-9 and 10 are the Report's other severity-and-threshold machinery (risk threshold, marginal risk, framework rows, systemic risks), which I count as acceptable; ranks 11-20 (risk identification, threat modelling, risk mitigation, a RLHF example table row, the Box 2.3 passage) are filler.
outline: Better than hybrid on the grade-2 set: #271 (L1528-1530) is opened along with the other three; only three grade-1 passages are not opened. 161 source lines are opened for 27 ranges. About half of the opened ranges are the generic risk-management machinery of section 3.2 (risk identification, tables, risk mitigation) which holds no graded passage. An agent reading it would see the chapter 2.2.2 and 3.4 ranges but not that the Report never defines the word; nothing in the outline says 'term used three times, never defined'.
